data.name: No Stick Shooter
data.detailed_description:
Happy Robot presents a fresh take on the classic retro-arcade shooters we all know and love. Featuring 30 levels of non-stop mayhem, a huge variety of enemies, strategic weaponry, and a unique control scheme, No Stick Shooter is packed full of explosive fun!



From simple asteroids to wiggly snakes and giant guns, No Stick Shooter delivers a wide range of enemies each with their own individual behaviors.



Discover the strengths and weaknesses of several unique weapons, each carefully designed to be as explosively satisfying as possible!

Carefully balance your enemies and weapons and devise the most effective approach to each challenge in order to achieve the highest scores and create the largest explosions! Fight your way through 30 challenging levels, including three boss fights and additional goals to achieve along the way.

reviews.review:
One of my favourite games on the old Atari systems was Asteroid. I’d spend hours as a small child playing the hell out of it. When I wasn’t playing, it I was watching my mother or a friend playing. We’d often have competitions to see who could do the best. When I first saw No Stick Shooter, developed by Happy Robot Games, had been released onto Steam I was hopeful that it would rekindle some of those memories.

[h1]First Impressions – It Didn’t Disappoint[/h1]

To be perfectly honest, I knew within the first handful of minutes that this was the game that I had been looking for. I was instantly hooked. Yet, this was another game that I was disappointingly poorly skilled in. Truth be told, I had set it up to be streamed on Twitch. But I knew almost right away that my skills weren’t of a sufficient standard to stream this for a stream worthy of watching. 

However, it’s certainly one of those games that engaged my mind. I wanted to strive for improvement. I turned off my Twitch stream and went about learning the game. I soon made some progress. I started unlocking achievements (something I always remove when reviewing so that in my free gaming time I can come back and enjoy the game and earn those achievements then!)

What caught my attention the most, right from the first level of the game, was that the game wasn’t going to hold my hands. This game throws three different enemy types at you in the opening level. There’s big ball clusters, the regular slower single asteroids as well as faster individual asteroids. The player is taught to immediately understand that there is going to be a significant amount of strategy as well as quick trigger fingers required to be successful at the game. This is a challenge I could get into!

[h1]Weapons[/h1]

The further you delve into the game the more weapons you unlock. What an absolute pleasure it is to unlock each new weapon. The game design decisions that have gone into the selections of the weaponry is very well done. Each of them is easily differentiated from one to the next. Each of them has their own unique strengths and weaknesses. Each of them makes complete and utter sense with regards to why you would have each weapon in the game. Of all the arcade and asteroids-like games I have played No Stick Shooter has me appreciating the design the most.  Kudos to Happy Robot Games for nailing one of the most important components of the genre. It’s their Steam debut, no less. 
Having completed most of a game design course myself, intelligent game design choices are still what impress me most. They are the little, yet highly significant choices, that transform a game from being mediocre into being very good. Yet they are so easy to get very wrong. It really goes to show that you don’t need to be a major studio to have people who truly understand how games work in today’s day and age. 

[h1]It’s a Challenge[/h1]

There was a level midway through the game where I was obliterating all of the objectives, 3 each level, and so I thought that I was going all guns’ blazes. That was true until towards the very end of the level I had fired so many shots that I was out of energy. One of the enemies that spawns a lot of tiny fragments shat all over my base with its evil demented spawn. Not only did I lose all my shields but my base exploded. Therefore, players need to be careful not only to cause the largest explosions but to preserve ammunition. Strategy in this game is every bit as important as action.
Consequently, dying isn’t something that is uncommon within the game. You’re going to die and you’re going to do it often. Each level feels rewarding when you complete it for the first time (except for the first level). This is without even focusing on getting the objectives complete. I would urge players to focus on completing the level for the first time and replaying the levels to complete the objectives. Somewhat delightfully, you don’t even have to complete the first task to unlock the next level. You simply must beat the level.  However, that’s easier said than done.
There are also boss fights. The boss fights are even more impressive than the standard levels. They are well designed battles that force the player to utilize all the tools and strategies that they have learned throughout the game. They made me feel like a high school student sitting important tests all over again. This was a very good and comfortable feeling when the challenge was defeated.

[h1]Presentation[/h1]

I really hate to say this but whoever was responsible for putting the Steam store page up, please try again. The screenshots that have been uploaded to the Steam store do not do your game justice. Although simple in design the game is much more visually pleasing than the screenshots show. While not state of the art by any means they are easy on the eye and are more than sufficient to get the job done. In fact, I was quite pleased with the visual representation. I feel that they capture the genre and the retro feel well while also giving the fresh take that gives the game a positive differential on the classic.

I’d also compliment the soundtrack of the game. It’s very befitting of the science fiction, space, theme that the game obviously has. It’s futuristic and again is very easy to listen to. The actual game sounds are a suitable choice as well. However, they are not the highlight of the presentation and are not at all memorable (but they needn’t be).

[h1]Steamified[/h1]

There are a set of Steam achievements with the game. However, I believe that the game has fallen victim to Valve’s new trading card program policy. I’m hopeful that the game will generate enough sales whereby the developer can add the game to the program. There is certainly a genuine amount of effort for potential buyers to follow through with a purchase. The game has been extremely well priced at just $2.99 on the US store and cheaper elsewhere (comparatively).
I would, however, suggest that the developers patch in Steam leaderboard support. This would give the game a much-needed shot in the arm with regards to competitive play. The objectives are challenging in and of themselves but I often wondered how much better the best players are than I. I’m certain that it’s by an embarrassingly large amount. But let me see it!

[h1]The No Stick Verdict[/h1]

Thank you, Happy Robot Games, for giving me a part of my childhood back. Although you’re not the original you have provided a highly challenging and addictive retro arcade, asteroids-like, experience. You’ve inspired friends who haven’t played video games in years to bend to the word of mouth pressure and give you a chance. So far, they’re only disappointed in the fact that you’ve stolen their free time. Such is the quality of the game at the price you have set. Kudos

Rating: 8/10
